<c>A</c>t that time: When Jesus was come near to Jerusalem, He beheld the city, and wept over it, saying: If thou hadst known, even thou, at least in this thy day, the things which belong unto thy peace! but now they are hid from thine eyes. And so on.

Homily by Pope St. Gregory the Great.
<r>39 on the Gospels.</r>
<c>N</c>o man that hath read the history of the destruction of Jerusalem by the Roman Princes Vespasian and Titus, can be ignorant that it was of that destruction that the Lord spoke when He wept over the ruin of the city. It is these Princes that are pointed at where it is said “For the days shall come upon thee that thine enemies shall cast a trench about thee.” The truth of what followeth: “They shall not leave in thee one stone upon another” is even now fulfilled in the change of site of the city, which hath been re-built round about that place without the gates, where the Lord was crucified, while the ancient city hath been, as I am told, rooted up from the very foundations.

<h>Martyrologium</h>
<c>Q</c>uartodécimo Kaléndas Augústi Luna quinta décima. Anno Dómini 2027
<h>S</h>ancti Vincéntii a Paulo, Presbýteri et Confessóris, Congregatiónis Presbyterórum Missiónis et Puellárum Caritátis Fundatóris, cæléstis ómnium caritátis Societátum Patróni; qui in Dómino obdormívit quinto Kaléndas Octóbris.
<h>C</h>olóssis, in Phrýgia, natális sancti Epaphræ, quem sanctus Paulus Apóstolus concaptívum appéllat. Hic, ab eódem Apóstolo Colóssis Epíscopus ordinátus, ibídem, clarus virtútibus, martýrii palmam, pro óvibus sibi commendátis, viríli agóne percépit; cujus corpus Romæ, in Basílica sanctæ Maríæ Majóris, cónditum est.
<h>T</h>réviris sancti Martíni, Epíscopi et Mártyris.
<h>H</h>íspali, in Hispánia, pássio sanctárum Vírginum Justæ et Rufínæ, quæ, a Prǽside Diogeniáno comprehénsæ, primo equúlei extensióne et ungulárum laniatióne vexátæ, póstea cárcere, inédia et váriis torsiónibus sunt afflíctæ; tandem Justa in cárcere spíritum exhalávit, Rufínæ vero cervix, in confessióne Dómini, confrácta est.
<h>C</h>órdubæ, in Hispánia, sanctæ Aureæ Vírginis, beatórum Adúlphi et Joánnis Mártyrum soróris; quæ aliquándo in apostasíæ crimen a Mahumetáno Júdice indúcta est, sed mox, facti pǽnitens, iteráto certámine, hostem effúso sánguine superávit.
<h>R</h>omæ sancti Sýmmachi Papæ, qui, a schismaticórum factióne diútius fatigátus, demum, sanctitáte conspícuus, migrávit ad Dóminum.
<h>V</h>erónæ sancti Felícis Epíscopi.
<h>A</h>pud Scetim, Ægýpti montem, sancti Arsénii, Románæ Ecclésiæ Diáconi; qui, Theodósii témpore, in solitúdinem secéssit, ibíque, virtútibus ómnibus consummátus et jugi lacrimárum imbre perfúsus, spíritum Deo réddidit.
<h>I</h>n Cappadócia sanctæ Macrínæ Vírginis, fíliæ sanctórum Basilíi et Emméliæ, atque soróris item sanctórum Episcopórum Basilíi Magni, Gregórii Nysséni et Petri Sebasténsis.

<h>Martyrology</h>
<c>J</c>uly 19th 2027, the 15th day of the Moon,
<h>O</h>n the morrow we keep the feast of the holy Confessor Vincent of Paul, who slept in the Lord upon the 27th day of September, and whom Pope Leo XIII. proclaimed the patron before God in heaven of all charitable societies throughout the whole Catholic world which derive their origin in any way from his institution, [in the year 1660.]
<h>U</h>pon the same 19th day of July, were born into the better life:
<h>T</h>he holy Epaphras, whom the holy Apostle Paul doth call his own fellow prisoner. He was ordained by the same Apostle Bishop of Colossi, where, illustrious for graces, he gained the palm of martyrdom in manly contending on behalf of the sheep committed to his care. His body is buried at Rome, in the Church of St Mary the greater.
<h>A</h>t Trier, the holy martyr Martin, Bishop [of that see, in the year 210.]
<h>A</h>t Seville, in Spain, the holy Virgins Justa and Rufina. They were arrested under the President Diogenian. They were first racked and tormented by being torn with hooks, and afterwards afflicted with imprisonment, starvation, and diverse tortures. In the end Justa gave up the ghost in prison, and Rufina had her neck broken for confessing the Lord, [at the end of the third century.]
<h>A</h>t Cordova, the holy Virgin Aurea, who for a time fell away, but repented of what she had done, and in a renewed combat prevailed against the enemy by the shedding of her blood, [in the year 856.]
<h>A</h>t Rome, the holy Pope Symmachus, who long suffered through the deeds of the schismatics, and at length passed away, famous for holiness, to be ever with the Lord, [in the year 514.]
<h>A</h>t Verona, holy Felix, the Bishop.
<h>A</h>t Mount Skete, in Egypt, holy Arsenius, a Deacon of the Church of Rome, who in the time of Theodosius betook himself to the desert, where he gave up his soul to God, finished in all graces and plentifully wet with tears, [in the year 450.]
<h>I</h>n Cappadocia, the holy Virgin Macrina, sister to holy Basil the Great and Gregory of Nyssa, [in the year 379.]
<r>℣.</r> And elsewhere many other holy martyrs, confessors, and holy virgins.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.
b.7ec082650b:
<h>Regula vel Evangelium</h>
<r>℣.</r> Jube, domne, benedícere.
Divínum auxílium ✠ máneat semper nobíscum.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.
<c>s</c>ecúndum Lucam
<r>Luc 19:41-47</r>
<c>I</c>n illo témpore: Cum appropinquáret Jesus Jerúsalem, videns civitátem, flevit super illam, dicens: Quia si cognovísses et tu, et quidem in hac die tua, quæ ad pacem tibi, nunc autem abscóndita sunt ab óculis tuis. Quia vénient dies in te: et circúmdabunt te inimíci tui vallo, et circúmdabunt te: et coangustábunt te úndique: et ad terram prostérnent te, et fílios tuos, qui in te sunt, et non relínquent in te lápidem super lápidem: eo quod non cognóveris tempus visitatiónis tuæ. Et ingréssus in templum, cœpit ejícere vendéntes in illo et eméntes, dicens illis: Scriptum est: Quia domus mea domus oratiónis est. Vos autem fecístis illam speluncam latrónum. Et erat docens cotídie in templo.
<r>℣.</r> Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nostri.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.
Commemorátio Fratrum, Sorórum, Familiárium, Benefactórum defunctórum Ordinis nostri.
Requiéscant in pace.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.

<r>Psalmus 116</r>
§11.66d6af014b
<r>℣.</r> Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
<r>℟.</r> Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.

<r>℣.</r> Osténde nobis, Dómine, misericórdiam tuam.
<r>℟.</r> Et salutáre tuum da nobis.

<r>℣.</r> Dómine, exáudi oratiónem meam.
<r>℟.</r> Et clamor meus ad te véniat.
<c>A</c>ctiónes nostras, quǽsumus, Dómine, aspirándo prǽveni et adiuvándo proséquere: ut cuncta nostra orátio et operátio a te semper incípiat, et per te cœpta finiátur.
Per Christum Dóminum nostrum.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.

<r>℣.</r> Adjutórium nostrum ✠ in nómine Dómini.
<r>℟.</r> Qui fecit cælum et terram.
<n>Si non sequitur aliqua Hora dicitur</n>
<r>℣.</r> Fidélium ánimæ per misericórdiam Dei requiéscant in pace.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.
b.eea71714c6:
<h>Regula vel Evangelium</h>
<r>℣.</r> Grant, Lord, a blessing.
May the divine assistance ✠ remain with us always.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.
<c>t</c>o Luke
<r>Luke 19:41-47</r>
<c>A</c>t that time, when Jesus drew near to Jerusalem and saw the city, He wept over it, saying, If you had known, in this your day, even you, the things that are for your peace! But now they are hidden from your eyes. For days will come upon you when your enemies will throw up a rampart about you, and surround you and shut you in on every side, and will dash you to the ground and your children within you, and will not leave in you one stone upon another, because you have not known the time of your visitation. And He entered the temple, and began to cast out those who were selling and buying in it, saying to them, It is written, ‘My house is a house of prayer,’ but you have made it a den of thieves. And He was teaching daily in the temple.
<r>℣.</r> But thou, O Lord, have mercy upon us.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.
Commemoration of the deceased Brethren, Sisters, Relations and Benefactors of our Order.
Requiéscant in pace.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.

<r>Psalm 116</r>
§11.0a67a14e81
<r>℣.</r> Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.
<r>℟.</r> As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

<r>℣.</r> Show us, O Lord, thy mercy.
<r>℟.</r> And grant us thy salvation.

<r>℣.</r> O Lord, hear my prayer.
<r>℟.</r> And let my cry come unto thee.
<c>D</c>irect, we beseech thee, O Lord, our actions by thy holy inspiration, and carry them on by thy gracious assistance: that every prayer and work of ours may always begin from thee, and by thee be happily ended.
Through Christ our Lord.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.

<r>℣.</r> Our help is ✠ in the name of the Lord,
<r>℟.</r> Who made heaven and earth.
<n>Si non sequitur aliqua Hora dicitur</n>
<r>℣.</r> May the souls of the faithful, through the mercy of God, rest in peace.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.

b.ae608b5bfc:
<h>Oratio</h>
<r>℣.</r> Dóminus vobíscum.
<r>℟.</r> Et cum spíritu tuo.
<c>O</c>rémus.
<c>P</c>áteant aures misericórdiæ tuæ, Dómine, précibus supplicántium: et, ut peténtibus desideráta concédas; fac eos, quæ tibi sunt plácita, postuláre.
<h>P</h>er Dóminum nostrum Jesum Christum, Fílium tuum: qui tecum vivit et regnat in unitáte Spíritus Sancti, Deus, per ómnia sǽcula sæculórum.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.
b.2c2ee70944:
<h>Prayer</h>
<r>℣.</r> The Lord be with you.
<r>℟.</r> And with thy spirit.
<c>L</c>et us pray.
<c>L</c>et thy merciful ears, O Lord, be open to the prayers of thy humble servants; and, that they may obtain their petitions, make them to ask such things as shall please thee.
<h>T</h>hrough Jesus Christ, thy Son our Lord, Who liveth and reigneth with thee, in the unity of the Holy Ghost, God, world without end.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.
